title: CAMS2_54b Co-design of GHG policy services in support of EU Member States and Copernicus Participating countries
description:
The successful bidder will propose the interaction with national inventory agencies and related institutes that are responsible for national monitoring of GHG emissions and the reporting to the UNFCCC . 
The successful Tenderer shall carry out the following activities:
•	Detailed familiarisation of the successful Tenderer with the latest status of current and emerging operational CAMS products and the use of satellite Earth Observations (EO) for GHG emissions monitoring. 
•	Facilitate collaboration between European national inventory agencies and CAMS. 
•	Collect, document and analyse user requirements at national level for EU member states and Copernicus participating countries. 
•	Provide recommendations for the development of policy-relevant tools, including data visualisation,  at national level.

title: UK Space Agency - Operational Support to the International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
description:
The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. 
Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/
Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. 
The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions.
